heroHeadline: Kast's Approval Craters to a Term-Low 30% as Foro Madrid Summit and Student-March Crackdown Fuel Backlash
heroSubtitle: President José Antonio Kast's approval collapsed through the first week of September: a Cadem poll fielded September 2 put him at 34% (61% disapproving) — already his lowest since taking office — before a Criteria poll fielded September 3–4 and published September 6 pushed the floor lower still, to 30% approval and 58% disapproval, with 52% saying the country is going backward. The slide coincided with Kast and Argentine President Javier Milei co-hosting the far-right Foro Madrid summit in Santiago (September 3–4), which drew protests in Santiago and Valparaíso alongside a separate Plaza Italia demonstration where police used tear gas and water cannon against crowds chanting that Kast is 'just like Pinochet' over his security reform; a further ACES-led march of 5,000+ students against education budget cuts was likewise broken up by Carabineros on September 3–4. Kast and Milei used the visit to jointly reaffirm Chilean sovereignty over the Strait of Magellan under the 1881 and 1984 treaties, resolving the diplomatic spat with Argentina, while on September 9 the government sent its MK4 capital-markets reform — housing down-payment aid, a BancoEstado mortgage fund and a new junior-mining exchange — to Congress with maximum urgency. Copper, meanwhile, closed September 8–9 at US$14,737/tonne, its second-highest level on record, as Chilean and Peruvian supply constraints met fresh US tariff fears.
footerNote: Data sourced from official Chilean government records (Biblioteca del Congreso, Banco Central, SERVEL), Rettig and Valech commissions, IACHR, CIPER Chile, and major international outlets.
